clips.title: The Most Important Skill for AI Engineers: Evals Explained
clips.why: The three ways to grade an AI system: people, code-based checks and model judges. Our bench grades mostly with code, and this clip shows why that is the strongest kind when it fits.
look: Code-based checks are cheap and never change their mind, but they only fit questions with a clear right answer.
Model judges help where the answer is fuzzy, and need checking themselves.
clips.after: A red-build case has clear answers, green or not, a false heal or not, paths inside the charter or not, so ROUTINE-BENCH grades it with code.

clips.title: Making Agent Evals Isn't As Hard As You Think!
clips.why: Benchmark evals for agents: a fixed set of tasks run again after every change, which is exactly what each slice of ROUTINE-BENCH is.
look: A benchmark is only useful if it stays fixed, so scores before and after a change can be compared.
Notice how agent runs vary, which is why we run every case three times.
clips.after: Every change to a routine's charter or skills re-runs its slice in CI, and the score appears on the pull request.

practice.q: Finish the rule for where a red-build case starts.
practice.before: A case starts at the first
practice.after: build of a streak, and its human fix is the next green one.
practice.hint: The colour of a failed CI run.
practice.why: Later red builds of the same streak are the same failure, so one streak gives one case.

practice.q: Where do a case's saved log, human fix and hidden tests live?

options.text: In the ai-agents repo, next to the case.yaml
options.why: Agents can read ai-agents. Answers stored there would leak into the routines they grade.

options.text: In the restricted golden-set repo that agents can never read
options.why: The answers stay where no agent can see them, the same place TICKET-BENCH keeps its answers.

options.text: In the R&D brain, so people can search them
options.why: The brain is searchable by agents too. The answers must never be indexed.

practice.q: Put the life of one red-build case in order.
items: Find the first red of a streak on main and the next green after it
Save the failed log, scrubbed with gitleaks, in the restricted golden-set repo
Write case.yaml with the base commit, the trigger and the grade
Run the routine on the case three times
Grade each run for green, honesty and paths, then compute pass@1 and pass^3
practice.why: History provides the case, the restricted repo protects the answer, and three graded runs turn it into a score.

practice.q: A bug fixer's new test fails on the base commit and also fails with the human fix applied. Is the bug reproduced?

options.why: Failing on base is only half. It must also pass with the human fix, or it found a different problem.

options.text: No, because it did not pass with the human fix, so it caught something other than the reported bug
options.why: Reproduced means: fails on base, passes with the human fix.

options.text: Only if the hidden tests also fail on base
options.why: The hidden tests are the human's. Reproduction is about the routine's own test.
